question.text:
The disjoint union $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup A_3 \sqcup A_4$ of events $A_1,A_2,A_3, A_4$ covers the entire sample space. Compute $P(A_2|B)$ given the following probabilities:

\begin{align*} & P(B|A_1)=0.25, & P(A_1)=0.28 \\[3pt] & P(B|A_2)=0.3, & \\[3pt] & P(B|A_3)=0.28, & P(A_3)=0.18 \\[3pt] & P(B|A_4)=0.1, & P(A_4)=0.22 \\[3pt] \end{align*}

Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
If the disjoint union $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup \ldots \sqcup A_n$ covers the entire sample space, Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability gives us the following:

\[ P(A_k | B) = \dfrac{P(B|A_k) P(A_k)}{P(B)} = \dfrac{P(B|A_k) P(A_k)}{\sum_{i=1}^n P(B|A_i)P(A_i)} \]

where $k=1,2,\ldots,n.$

In our case, $n=4,$ and $A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup A_3 \sqcup A_4$ covers the entire sample space. Consequently, we have

\[ P(A_1) + P(A_2) + P(A_3) + P(A_4) = 1. \]

As a result,

\begin{align*} P(A_2) &= 1 - (P(A_1)+P(A_3)+P(A_4)) \\[3pt] &= 1 - (0.28+0.18+0.22) \\[3pt] &= 0.32. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} P(A_2 | B) &= \dfrac{P(B|A_2) P(A_2)}{\sum_{i=1}^4 P(B|A_i)P(A_i)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(B|A_2) P(A_2)}{P(B|A_1)P(A_1) + P(B|A_2)P(A_2) + P(B|A_3)P(A_3)+ P(B|A_4)P(A_4)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{(0.3) (0.32)}{(0.25)(0.28) + (0.3)(0.32) + (0.28)(0.18)+ (0.1)(0.22)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.096}{0.2384} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.403. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing a Conditional Probability Using Bayes' Theorem

question.text:
An English teacher believes that students who prefer cursive handwriting tend to perform better in essay writing. To prove his belief, he puts some students into groups of three according to their average writing grades and asks them if they usually write in cursive.

  • $20\%$ of students have low grades, and $12\%$ of those students usually write in cursive.
  • $65\%$ of students have average grades, and $15\%$ of those students usually write in cursive.
  • $15\%$ of students have high grades, and $17\%$ of those students usually write in cursive.

If $56\%$ of students are female, and $16\%$ of female students write in cursive, what is the probability that a randomly chosen student who writes in cursive is a female? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a student is female, $W$ be the event that the student writes in cursive, and $L, A, H$ be the events that the student has low, average, or high grades, respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(L) = 0.2 && P(W | L) = 0.12 \\[3pt] & P(A) = 0.65 && P(W | A) = 0.15 \\[3pt] & P(H) = 0.15 && P(W | H) = 0.17 \end{align*} The disjoint union $L \sqcup A \sqcup H$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(L)+ P(A) + P(H) = 0.2+0.65+0.15 = 1. \]

  • Since $56\%$ of students are female, we have \[ P(F) = 0.56. \]

  • Since $16\%$ of female students write in cursive, we have \[ P(W | F) = 0.16. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen student who writes in cursive is a female, which is represented as $P(F | W).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(F | W) &= \dfrac{P(W | F) P(F)}{P(W)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(W | F) P(F)}{P(W | L) P(L) + P(W | A) P(A) + P(W | H) P(H)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (0.16)(0.56) }{ (0.2)(0.12) + (0.65)(0.15) + (0.15)(0.17)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.0896}{0.147} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.610, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Applying Bayes’ Theorem to a Situation in Context

question.text:
A medical center is investigating the correlation between scoliosis and sports practice in a sample of children.

  • $25\%$ of children in the sample don't practice sports, and $3\%$ of those children have scoliosis.
  • $30\%$ of children in the sample practice one sport, and $2.5\%$ of those children have scoliosis.
  • $45\%$ of children in the sample practice two sports, and $3.3\%$ of those children have scoliosis.

If $52\%$ of children in the entire sample are female, and $2\%$ of female children have scoliosis, what is the probability that a randomly chosen child with scoliosis is female? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a child is female, $C$ be the event that a child has scoliosis, and $S_0, S_1, S_2$ be the event that a child practice $0,$ $1,$ or $2$ sports, respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(S_0) = 0.25 && P(C | S_0) = 0.03 \\[3pt] & P(S_1) = 0.30 && P(C | S_1) = 0.025 \\[3pt] & P(S_2) = 0.45 && P(C | S_2) = 0.033 \end{align*} The disjoint union $S_0 \sqcup S_1 \sqcup S_2$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(S_0)+ P(S_1) + P(S_2) = 0.25+0.30+0.45 = 1. \]

  • Since $52\%$ of children in the entire sample are female, we have \[ P(F) = 0.52. \]

  • Since $2\%$ of females have scoliosis, we have \[ P(C | F) = 0.02. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen child with scoliosis is female, which is represented as $P(F | C).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(F | C) &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F)}{P(C)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(C | F) P(F) }{P(C | S_0) P(S_0) + P(C | S_1) P(S_1) + P(C | S_2) P(S_2)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (0.02)(0.52) }{ (0.03)(0.25) + (0.025)(0.3) + (0.033)(0.45)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.0104}{0.0299} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.348, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Applying Bayes’ Theorem to a Situation in Context

question.text:
A gambling room has three roulette tables, table $1,$ table $2,$ and table $3.$ Data of all bets of a particular evening are collected.

  • $30\%$ of bets were played at table $1,$ and $5\%$ of those bets were won.
  • $35\%$ of bets were played at table $2,$ and $6\%$ of those bets were won.
  • $35\%$ of bets were played at table $3,$ and $7\%$ of those bets were won.

If $10\%$ of bets were played in the first hour, and $4\%$ of bets made in the first hour were won, what is the probability that a randomly chosen winning bet was played in the first hour? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a bet is played in the first hour, $W$ be the event that a bet is won, and $T_1, T_2, T_3$ be the events that a bet is played at table $1,$ $2,$ or $3,$ respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(T_1) = 0.3 && P(W | T_1) = 0.05 \\[3pt] & P(T_2) = 0.35 && P(W | T_2) = 0.06 \\[3pt] & P(T_3) = 0.35 && P(W | T_3) = 0.07 \end{align*} The disjoint union $T_1 \sqcup T_2 \sqcup T_3$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(T_1)+ P(T_2) + P(T_3) = 0.3+0.35+0.35 = 1. \]

  • Since $10\%$ of bets in the entire evening are played in the first hour, we have \[ P(F) = 0.1. \]

  • Since $4\%$ of bets made in the first hour are won, we have \[ P(W | F) = 0.04. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen winning bet is played in the first hour, which is represented as $P(F | W).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

\begin{align*} P(F | W) &= \dfrac{P(W | F) P(F)}{P(W)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{P(W | F) P(F) }{P(W | T_1) P(T_1) + P(W | T_2) P(T_2) + P(W | T_3) P(T_3)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (0.04)(0.1) }{ (0.05)(0.3) + (0.06)(0.35) + (0.07)(0.35)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{0.004}{0.0605} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.066, \end{align*}

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

example.title: Applying Bayes’ Theorem to a Situation in Context

question.text:
A medical center is investigating the correlation between scoliosis and sports practice in a sample of children.

  • $25\%$ of children in the sample don't practice sports, and $2.5\%$ of those children have scoliosis.
  • $30\%$ of children in the sample practice one sport.
  • $45\%$ of children in the sample practice two sports, and $2.8\%$ of those children have scoliosis.

If $48\%$ of children in the entire sample are female, $2.6\%$ of female children have scoliosis, and $46\%$ of children with scoliosis are female, what is the probability that a randomly chosen child who practices one sport has scoliosis? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Let $F$ be the event that a child is female, $C$ be the event that a child has scoliosis, and $S_0, S_1, S_2$ be the event that a child practices $0,$ $1,$ or $2$ sports, respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: \begin{align*} & P(S_0) = 0.25 && P(C \mid S_0) = 0.025 \\[5pt] & P(S_1) = 0.30 \\[5pt] & P(S_2) = 0.45 && P(C \mid S_2) = 0.028 \end{align*} The disjoint union $S_0 \sqcup S_1 \sqcup S_2$ covers the entire sample space, and we have \[ P(S_0) + P(S_1) + P(S_2) = 0.25 + 0.30 + 0.45 = 1. \]

  • Since $48\%$ of students in the entire sample are female, we have \[ P(F) = 0.48. \]

  • Since $2.6\%$ of females have scoliosis, we have \[ P(C \mid F) = 0.026. \]

  • Since $46\%$ of children with scoliosis are female, we have \[ P(F \mid C) = 0.46. \]

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen child who practices one sport has scoliosis, which is represented as $P(C \mid S_1).$

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have \begin{align*} P(F \mid C) &= \dfrac{P(C \mid F) P(F)}{P(C)} \\[5pt] P(F \mid C) &= \dfrac{P(C \mid F) P(F)}{P(C \mid S_0) P(S_0) + P(C \mid S_1) P(S_1) + P(C \mid S_2) P(S_2)} \\[5pt] 0.46 &= \dfrac{(0.026)(0.48)}{(0.25)(0.025) + P(C \mid S_1)(0.3) + (0.028)(0.45)} \\[5pt] 0.46 &= \dfrac{0.0125}{0.0189 + 0.3P(C \mid S_1)} \end{align*}

Solving this equation for $P(C \mid S_1),$ we have \begin{align*} 0.46(0.0189 + 0.3P(C \mid S_1)) &= 0.0125 \\[5pt] 0.0189 + 0.3P(C \mid S_1) &= \dfrac{0.0125}{0.46} \\[5pt] 0.3P(C \mid S_1) &= \dfrac{0.0125}{0.46} - 0.0189 \\[5pt] P(C \mid S_1) &= \dfrac{1}{0.3} \left( \dfrac{0.0125}{0.46} - 0.0189 \right) \\[5pt] P(C \mid S_1) &\approx 0.028 \end{align*}

rounded to three decimal places.
